matches.rationale: Both identify that the abstract cherry-picks favorable FID scores (2.38–2.64) while omitting substantial degradation at higher replacement ratios. GT notes Table 4 shows FID > 3.6 at 75% and failures at 100%; pred_id 1 notes the abstract claims 2.15–2.38 and 'consistently outperforms' which is contradicted by Table 4 showing failures (e.g., Hyena-SE 100% FID 8.23, Hyena-X 75% FID 3.69).

GT concerns ambiguity in Equation 2's regression objective L_reg and the conditioning variable c in Section 3.1/3.3. None of the findings address this methodological inconsistency about the distillation loss formulation or the role of conditioning variables.

GT identifies missing hyperparameter details in Table C.1 (gradient clipping specification, warmup schedule details, batch size clarification). None of the findings mention Table C.1 or these specific protocol omissions.

GT concerns overstated claims in the Introduction about grafting 'proving' utility and generalizing beyond tested models. While pred_id 7 addresses overstated conclusion claims, it focuses on different language ('completely solves,' 'universally outperforms') in Section 7, not the Introduction claims identified in GT.

Both identify selective omission of actual FID values in Table 4 using '✗' markers and ambiguity about what ΔFLOPs measures. GT notes '✗' denotes FID > 50 without actual values and confusion between ΔFLOPs_op and ΔFLOPs_ft; pred_id 5 notes inconsistent thresholds (50/75/140) for the same condition and the '✗' marker issue.

GT identifies fabricated relevance of reference [4] (plant grafting paper) in the Introduction footnote. None of the findings address this specific reference misattribution or the horticultural grafting analogy.

Both identify inconsistency in Section 3.4's locality metric interpretation. GT notes the text claims 'L_k > 0.5 for 15 out of 28 layers' but questions whether this meaningfully indicates local attention given averaging. Pred_id 2 identifies direct contradiction: text says 'all 28 layers > 0.7' while Figure 2 caption says 'only 15 of 28 layers > 0.5' for k=32.

GT concerns unfair comparison in Section 5 GenEval results due to potentially different sampling steps or LoRA vs. full finetuning between baseline and grafted PixArt-Σ. None of the findings address this specific experimental protocol issue about evaluation fairness.

Both identify misleading comparison in Table 6 where the grafted model (FID 2.77, 712M params) is claimed to outperform baselines. GT notes it's compared to TinyDiT-D14 (340M params) unfairly and doesn't actually beat DiT-XL/2 (2.27). Pred_id 3 notes Section 6 claims it 'surpasses even the original DiT-XL/2 (FID=2.27)' but Table 6 shows 2.77 > 2.27, reversing the evidence.

GT concerns omission of limitations and failure cases in the Conclusion (e.g., 100% replacement failures, PixArt-Σ artifacts, bias risks). While pred_id 7 addresses overstated conclusion claims, it focuses on unsupported 'universally outperforms' language rather than the specific omission of acknowledged limitations.

Both identify selective reporting of latency measurements in Table 5. GT notes the unusual batch size=2 choice without justification or reporting at other batch sizes, and missing GPU utilization/throughput metrics. Pred_id 6 identifies that the reported 1.43× speedup doesn't match Table 5's actual data (1.59×).

Both identify inconsistency between abstract's claim about compute budget and actual experimental details. GT notes abstract claims '<2% compute' but best results use 20% data (not 10% as in Table C.1). Pred_id 4 identifies text in Section 3.3 claiming 'FID 2.53 with 10% data' but Table 2 shows 2.49 for that configuration, with 2.53 corresponding to a different setup.

GT concerns inappropriate promotional language ('revolutionary,' 'paradigm shift,' 'unprecedented') in the Introduction. None of the findings address rhetorical manipulation or overly promotional language in the paper.

GT identifies incorrect FLOP calculation formula in Section H.1 and inconsistency with reported ΔFLOPs_op reductions in Table 4. None of the findings address the appendix FLOP calculations or mathematical errors in the formulas.

GT identifies misrepresentation of reference [52] in Appendix A Related Work, which focuses on few-shot learning rather than architectural editing. None of the findings address this specific reference misattribution in the related work section.
